reading.rtitle: Who I Am and What I Do
paras: Good morning. Before I say what I do, let me say where I do it, because the two things are difficult to separate.

We are one group with three companies in South America. The bank holds the licence and provides services to the whole structure. The finance company works with the dealer network and with the customer: it finances the cars in the showroom and it finances the person who buys them. The rental company works with corporate clients who want to use cars and not to own them. Three companies, three clients, three countries: Brazil, Argentina and Chile.

My role sits across all of them. I am the HR business partner for the three entities, which means I am responsible for the people agenda in each one: the headcount, the hiring decisions, the performance cycle and the cost of the teams. I report to the global HR director at headquarters, and I have a dotted-line reporting to the regional managing director here. My stakeholders are the local managers, finance, compliance and, of course, the employees themselves.

A normal morning starts with the inbox. I go through it before the first meeting and I decide what the priority is: a request that needs a decision, an issue that belongs to another team, a policy update that only needs to be read. Then the decisions. Most of them are yes with a condition, or not yet, because something is still missing.

Let me give you one real example, without names. A manager asks for a position during a hiring freeze. I check the criteria, I ask for the workload and the cost, I take the business case to my manager and, if it is critical, to the CFO. The answer travels back the same way. When the answer is no, I say it clearly and I leave a date: we look at the position again in January.

One last point, and I say it on purpose. Payroll operations are not in my scope. A shared services team takes care of that, and knowing where my work starts and ends is part of doing it well. To sum up: three entities, three countries, one people agenda, and one person who connects headquarters to the managers.

listenings.text: Good morning. My name is not important for this exercise, so let me go straight to what I do. I am an HR business partner. I take care of recruitment, I take care of performance, I take care of the budget of the teams, and I also take care of the policies that come from headquarters. I work with three companies. I have meetings every day with managers, and I answer many requests. I also participate in projects, for example the onboarding project and the engagement survey. In addition, I support the managers in difficult conversations, and I prepare reports for the committee every month. That is more or less my job. It is a busy job, with many responsibilities, and I think that is everything.

Good morning. Before I say what I do, let me say where I do it. We are one group with three companies. The finance company finances the cars in the dealer showroom and the customer who buys them. The rental company works with corporate fleets. The bank holds the licence and serves the whole structure. Three companies, three clients, three countries. My role sits across all of them: I am responsible for the people agenda in each entity, and I report to the global HR director. Here is one example. During a hiring freeze, a manager asks for a position. I check the criteria, I ask for the workload and the cost, and I take the case to the CFO. If the answer is no, I say it clearly and I leave a date. And one thing that is not mine: payroll operations belong to shared services. I say that on purpose, because knowing where my work ends is part of doing it well.
